public_rationale: Repeated surveys provide directional evidence of greater concern about AI and insufficient oversight. Some attitudes were unchanged. These surveys do not isolate both targets of Marcus's claim or establish the full-year outcome. No decisive event meets the early-resolution rule, so the forecast remains pending through December 31, 2026.
limitations: General AI attitudes are an imperfect proxy for backlash against generative AI.
Wanting more regulation does not necessarily mean opposing a particular deregulation measure.
Polling and organized opposition measure different aspects of backlash.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: In 2026, public backlash against generative AI and radical AI deregulation will escalate.

statement.excerpt: Backlash to Generative AI and radical deregulation will escalate.
statement.document_title: Six (or seven) predictions for AI 2026 from a Generative AI realist

our_interpretation: The plain reading is increased public and organized opposition during 2026 compared with 2025.
Backlash applies to both generative AI and deregulation; the sentence does not separately predict that deregulation itself will increase.
The adjoining references to US midterms and Trump make US evidence the primary focus, although the sentence specifies no geography.
Radical is the speaker's characterization. Relevant evidence concerns opposition to removing or blocking AI safeguards.
The separate election and Trump predictions are outside this claim.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evidence shows a clear increase in public or organized opposition to generative AI and to removal of AI safeguards during 2026 relative to 2025.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence covering 2026 shows no broad increase, or a decline, in opposition to the named targets.

evidence.explanation: The May survey reports increased negative views of AI compared with 2025. It measures AI generally, not generative AI or opposition to a specific deregulation policy, so it is directional context.

Dissatisfaction with business transparency was largely unchanged, while the adjacent regulation comparison reports increased dissatisfaction with government oversight. The findings therefore do not show uniform escalation across all attitudes, and they do not isolate opposition to deregulation.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable 2025–2026 polling and documented organized or legislative opposition showing whether backlash increased against both generative AI and removal of AI safeguards.
